chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Isa Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

When the fifth [Imam] from the offspring of the seventh of the Imams is lost, then be careful of Allah regarding your religions; let no one remove you from it. O my sons, indeed the master of this affair must have an occultation, until those who used to affirm it will renounce it. It is merely a trial from Allah, with which Allah the Exalted tested His creation.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the occultation as a trial for believers according to Musa ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* identifies the 'fifth from the seventh' as Imam al-Hasan al-Askari, linking his occultation to a divine trial (*muhannah*) where believers are tested by the wavering of those who previously affirmed the Imamate. It underscores the necessity of steadfastness in faith during the period of absence, a core tenet of Twelver Shia eschatology.
